correctness.rationale: Energy-orthogonal vertex-interpolation/Dirichlet-bridge decomposition proves the general exact edgewise diagonal (1). Explicit hub/rim Fourier modes give H_h=9/(16m), H_r=u_m-15/(16m), R_spoke=u_m and R_rim=1-u_m. Rim and spoke profiles are strictly concave. For m>=4, F(u,1/m) is increasing in u on [4/9,1/2] and decreasing in x=1/m on [0,1/4], hence exceeds 37/5184; this yields the strict rim localization and a uniform gap. For m=3 all six K4 edge midpoints maximize. Exact gamma-free cyclic resolvent gives the limiting constant. A second independent centered Kirchhoff PDE construction verified 99 exact rational test evaluations, which are not substituted for the universal proof.

originality.rationale: Bapat and Gupta 2010 already obtain wheel vertex resistances, so they are excluded from novelty. Baker and Faber supply general metric-graph Green techniques and Cinkir the canonical-measure tau formula. Relevant primary full texts and named published-finding corpus/own-ledger claims were compared by mathematical implication: none established the present sharp unnormalized-arclength H1 wheel formula, all-point extremizer set or uniform rim/spoke separation. Bibliographic priority still carries residual risk.
residual_risks: Search results and examined literature cannot exclude an unindexed prior centered-Green sharp wheel calculation under another terminology.
Previously published Bapat–Gupta resistance identities imply the resolvent component of the formula, but no inspected source makes the additional nontrivial maximizer comparison.
Some tangential older Sobolev approximation literature was accessible only as bibliographic abstracts; its reported main subject is approximation numbers rather than exact wheel point evaluation.

value.rationale: An infinite, highly natural two-edge-orbit graph family gets a closed-form exact all-point Sobolev embedding constant, a complete equality classification, and a dimension-independent positive gap excluding spoke extremizers once m>=4. The exceptional tetrahedral boundary and the sqrt(5)/4 limit with exact inverse-m correction expose nontrivial structural localization and finite-size scaling. This is motivated by metric-graph sharp stability, not an arbitrary finite numerical slice.
